approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (General Charges Imposition) Bill 2025
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill is part of a package of three bills that together create a legal basis for charging fees related to activities under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
The specific activities and fee amounts would be set by regulations, and the minister must ensure those fees do not exceed the government's expected costs for handling those matters.

The package splits the charging rules into three separate laws because the Australian Constitution requires different types of taxes to be in different acts, with this bill covering charges that are neither customs nor excise duties.
The package establishes a framework for imposing charges on prescribed activities under the EPBC Act.
The package limits charges to cost recovery, requiring the minister to confirm that fee amounts will not over-recover the Commonwealth's likely expenses.
The package provides for collection and recovery of charges through amendments to the EPBC Act, as set out in the Environment Protection Reform Bill 2025.
The people and businesses that undertake activities regulated under the EPBC Act, and the Commonwealth agencies that administer those regulations.

Moved the second reading of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (General Charges Imposition) Bill 2025, which would establish cost-recovery charges for prescribed matters connected with administering the Act, with activities and amounts set by regulation after consultation.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to expedite debate and voting on seven environment bills, including limiting consideration in detail to five minutes per amendment set unless extended by a minister, and moved that the question be put.

Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders and set the day's business, including immediate consideration of the Environment Protection Reform Bill and related bills, specified times for second reading and remaining stages, permitted divisions after 4.30 pm, and subsequent consideration of listed Senate business.
